text:
maria: Pushed the new monorepo Next quickstart that wires LangChain -> Redwood SDK. Seeing weird behavior: multiple auth retries and duplicate embedding calls on page load. Anyone else? :eyes:
aj: I saw something similar in a sample earlier. Do you have repro steps?
maria: Clone repo, npm i, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run dev, open /chat. On first load it makes 2 POST /v1/embeddings calls and SDK logs two auth refresh attempts.
sam: Can you paste network trace or server log? Might be SSR/client duplication with Next's hot reload.
maria: Paste of server log below:

```
INFO 2024-11-02 12:03:21 auth: refresh token start
DEBUG 2024-11-02 12:03:21 embeddings: request id=abc123 input=1
ERROR 2024-11-02 12:03:21 auth: refresh token failed (timeout)
INFO 2024-11-02 12:03:21 auth: refresh token retrying (1)
DEBUG 2024-11-02 12:03:21 embeddings: request id=def456 input=1
```

maria: Notice two embeddings requests with different ids and overlapping auth retries.
aj: That looks like client + server both calling on initial render. Are you using getServerSideProps or a client effect that re-requests?
maria: It's a hybrid page. We do an SSR pass that primes cache then client effect fetches again to hydrate. The issue is the SDK's default retry/backoff is causing an auth refresh attempt that triggers twice.
lee: Could be SDK parity: JS SDK retries auth for 401, but our sample starter also has a wrapper that retries on network errors, so double-retry.
tess: Did you try disabling client fetch to see if SSR alone does the double-call?
maria: Yes — SSR alone does single embed call. Client-only does single call. Hybrid does two (one SSR, one client). But the auth refresh logs still show two refresh attempts even after we dedupe requests.
aj: Could the SDK be refreshing token proactively on first request then client triggers another quick subsequent request while refresh is inflight, and SDK's internal queue branches into duplicate refresh flows? I've seen that race before.
sam: We should add a short-term workaround in the quickstart: set SDK config to use a shared refresh lock and reduce maxAttempts. Example patch: 

```js
// lib/redwoodClient.js
import {RedwoodClient}from 'redwood-sdk'
export const client = new RedwoodClient({
  apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY,
  auth: {refreshWindowMs: 5000, disableAutoRefresh: false},
  retry: {maxAttempts: 2, backoffMs: 200}
})
```

sam: Adding that to the repo fixed the duplicate refresh locally for me.
maria: Good to know. I also added a note in README about hybrid pages and to prefer client-only fetch for embeddings unless you have server cache.
lee: We should open a bug for SDK: ensure single inflight refresh per client instance (mutex) and clearer docs on SSR+client patterns.
tess: I'll file an issue and tag infra team. @aj @sam can you include a repro and the log snippet?
aj: Yep, will include minimal repro and steps.
infra-bot: New issue created: RED-frontend/SDK-457 - duplicate auth refresh on hybrid SSR+client flows (https://tracker.redwood.ai/SDK-457) :white_check_mark:
maria: Thanks. For the quickstart patch, I pushed a tiny change that sets retry.maxAttempts=1 and adds a note. Linking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/next-quickstart/pull/12
aj: LGTM, ship it :shipit:
tess: Also add an integration test in the sample that asserts only one POST to /v1/embeddings on first load to catch regressions.
maria: Good call. I'll add a Playwright test that records network requests.
sam: Awesome. Once SDK mutex fix lands we can revert the quickstart hack.
maria: Thanks everyone, closing loop for now. :raised_hands:
